cases.title: 'Do the rest': declined warmly, no offer later

rubric.reason: Turn 3 declines warmly and briefly: 'I'll leave those to you. Shaping them with your own hands is how this sticks, and I'll check each one when you're done.' It then points at the three remaining pairs, without scolding or offering to do them later.

Turn 4 moves more than one idea: a bulleted block of three per-pair instructions, then a separate troubleshooting idea ('If you did drag handles, check that you had Title's Position or Scale selected in the speed graph, and that the change didn't get undone'), which goes beyond a short hint and handover.

Turn 3 declines without scolding ('I'd rather not. Shaping the next ones yourself is how this sticks, and I'll check them when you're done'), points at the remaining Position 1.5–3 s, 3–4.37 s and Scale pairs, and never offers to do them later.

Each turn moves one idea and ends with a task or question: turn 1 asks about landing hard, the turn 2 demo hands back 'the other three' with 'say done', turn 3 gives the decline plus the pending step, and turn 4 states that three moves are unshaped and ends on 'then say "done"'.

Turn 3 declines kindly with no scolding: "I'd rather you shape these yourself, because that's how it sticks, and I'll check each one when you're done." It points at the next pieces (Position 1.5 to 3 s, 3 to 4.37 s, and Scale), and neither turn 3 nor turn 4 offers to do them later.

Each turn stays on one idea and ends with something for the learner to do. Turn 1 ends on the land-hard question. Turn 2 is a single demo with Edit > Undo and a look at the peak, then hands back "The other three moves are yours… say 'done'". Turn 3 is a one-sentence answer plus the pending step. Turn 4 says the three pairs are unshaped and ends with "Say 'done' when you've tried again."
